title: Why he avoided the Schillinger system
summary: He sampled Schillinger through other writers, liked the harmonies but disliked a prefabricated method.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: It was about that time if my memory serves me right that the Schillinger system was very popular, or at least talked about a good deal. Did you ever brush against that?

No. I brushed against the Schillinger system by being associated with other guys that were writing for some of the rehearsal bands that I was writing for, who were using that system, and appreciating the beautiful harmonic changes that the system produced--
Do you remember exactly what it consisted of?

It seems to me, if I remember correctly, that there was a formula, if you wanted a mood of such and such, there were ways that you could refer to the formula and figure out how to get a green mood or a blue mood.
Exactly. And that turned me off.
It was a forerunner of computer music.

Right. I felt that it wasn't a live thing if it didn't grow from its own seed and develop of itself. If it was already created and lying in a drawer to be pulled out and used, I didn't want any part of it, so I avoided the Schillinger system. I took a quick look at it, felt that I understood what it was doing, I appreciated what it was producing; I didn't like the way it was being produced.
